newsitem.title: INDIA: Cricket-India's Dalmiya to be new ICC chief.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-India's Dalmiya to be new ICC chief.

text.p: India's Jagmohan Dalmiya will be the next head of the International Cricket Council (ICC) for a three-year term after the retirement of Sir Clyde Walcott in June, India's cricket board chief said on Tuesday.
"The working committee has already decided on Mr Jagmohan Dalmiya," Raj Singh Dungarpur, president of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), told Reuters by telephone from Bombay.

ICC chief executive David Richards said in Kuala Lumpur on Monday that India would take over at the head of the ICC in June and had until May 31 to name their choice for the new post of ICC president which will replace the chairman's job.

Dungarpur said the Indian board's committee had decided on Dalmiya as the country's chosen nominee last month, before the ICC decided in Kuala Lumpur that India would name the next ICC chief after the retirement of Barbadian Walcott.
Dalmiya's ascent to the top ICC post came after a heated debate last year over the council's electoral process that stood on the verge of a legal battle threatened by Indian officials.
Dalmiya, who is BCCI secretary, played a key role in organising the World Cup jointly hosted by India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka last year.
A construction magnate by profession, he has also been aggressively promoting the idea of commercial sponsorships for cricket and taking the game to more countries.
The game is now played mainly in a limited number of Commonwealth nations once ruled by Britain.
The president's post was part of a new governing structure aimed at improving the management and development of international cricket, Richards said.
India were unanimously elected to provide the president until June 2000 at a special general meeting of the ICC on Sunday.
Australia were elected as successors to India after 2000. The Australian candidate would serve as vice-president from June 1999, before taking over as president.
Last July, Dalmiya contested the chairmanship and was backed by full members Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe, besides a majority of the 22 associate members.
Test-playing nations, called full members, have two votes against one for associate members.
Dalmiya secured 25 votes against 13 for Australia's Malcolm Gray after South African Krish Mackerdhuj withdrew from the contest at the end of a first ballot.

But Dalmiya's bid was thwarted by England and Australia, who cited ICC rules to insist that a winning candidate needed the support of at least two-thirds of ICC's full members, meaning six out of the nine test- playing nations.
They were supported by New Zealand and West Indies.
Indian officials then contemplated court action, seeking a simple majority vote in ICC's elections.
ICC then decided that the election be postponed for a year and asked Walcott to continue as chairman.
On Monday, ICC decided to offer India the opportunity to take over the new post at the head of the Council in a new governing structure.
